cells.tense: You are inside the long practice right now, and it is holding.
cells.ask: Write one name for what you keep circling and leave it where you can see it.
cells.core:
You're inside the long practice now. Nothing flashy is holding it — just attention, kept on the same thing until it changes. The pattern you've been working around has started going quiet at the edges, and you're meeting that without pushing.

There's a certain way some things won't get said in the practice. You have people close at hand and moments where you could let something be understood and not handled — those mostly go unused, because the practice doesn't ask for them. The ground under this is real, and it has room in it. Writing one name for what you keep circling, and leaving it where you can see it, sits alongside the practice instead of replacing it.
cells.sheetLine: The same thing keeps changing because you keep showing up for it.
cells.verb: going deep enough into a pattern that thinking reaches its own edge
cells.place: where skill is built by repeating it alone, attention keeping the light on

cells.tense: You are racing a result that has not been written yet.
cells.ask: Write the pattern in five plain lines and say them to one person today, no revision.
cells.core:
You're working toward a version of this that hasn't happened, and it's bending the practice toward the result. Repetition was the point once — now you keep checking how deep you're getting, and the check pulls you up short before the work can settle.

What's underneath is being wrong at the end, having gone all the way in and found no ground. So you build the case for the depth while you're standing in it, and the building eats the thing it was for. Further along, the work would show itself on its own and you'd say what you've found where people could use it. Dial back the watching by one step a day. Put it in plain words for someone to hear now — flat, unfinished, fine — and they'll get the shape you're reaching for.

cells.tense: You stopped drawing on what you know, and the sitting has been quiet since.
cells.ask: Once this week, show one person a thing you know how to do, and say what you keep doing it for.
cells.core:
The sitting stayed but the going-in stopped. The middle of the practice runs on its own now, and less of you is home in it than there used to be. What you know is still filed and still true. It just doesn't get carried up into the room.

You're not short on ability. You're short on the aliveness that only comes when the work matters to someone else. That charge is what pulls the current through the quiet stretch. One person this week — do the thing in front of them and say out loud what you keep doing it for. It doesn't need to be your best work. It needs a witness.

cells.tense: You are already serving something with the practice and you keep calling it open.
cells.ask: Say out loud, once, what your practice serves and how you already stand behind it.
cells.core:
Done right, the depth comes from understanding rather than effort — a pattern shows itself, and seeing it loosens something instead of tightening it. You're near that. What lags is saying it. The practice hums along, and when someone asks what it's for, the words come slower than the work does.

There's a pull you follow when you sit down, and you've been filing it under just practicing. That lets it go unnamed for another stretch. The direction is already in how you work. Saying it aloud is a different muscle. Say plainly, without rehearsing, what the practice serves and how you already work toward it. That's not a vow. It's just paper.

attempts.check: The record doesn't support saying what the person is like at depth, why they keep practicing, or whether anything from the past made them this way — only how the capacity is behaving in one part of life now. A reader could reasonably say 'I'm not that consistent' or 'this isn't about practice,' so the sitting has to be one they could decline without the reading collapsing, and each ask has to be worth doing even if the read is wrong. The sentence that serves me more than them would be any line praising the practice itself instead of handing the authorship back; it's cut.
